description: Make each report a FULLY SELF-CONTAINED template that OWNS its own structure and its own complete styling per report type, fed only PURE DATA (from FEAT-002), and reproduces its reference PDF faithfully cell-by-cell: correct fonts (by name), sizes, weights, per-cell/column fill colours (the DIVISION PERFORMANCE / SUMMARY / GPA / TOTAL washes and the competency band), true row heights, alignment, rotated rank labels, and the exact structure/grouping - matching the reference so left and right compare identically. Dismantle the shared-CSS + reusable/generic-template coupling: no shared DOC_CSS/TEMPLATE_CSS constant funneling every report, no shared chrome funnel, no font-size clamp, no cross-report harmonization. Because DATA carries no styles, each report type's template ENCODES its own faithful presentation (the report type's design is fixed chrome that the template owns) and computes data-derived colour (competency) deterministically from the data. Start with schools_rank (the report in the user's screenshot), get it matching, then apply the same self-contained treatment to every family. Depends on FEAT-002; blocks FEAT-004.
steps: PRINCIPLE: styling + structure now live in the template, keyed to the report TYPE (the design is fixed furniture for that report type), and the template is fed PURE data. The reference for what each report type should look like is the original PDF and the conversion path's faithful output (src/sars/html_out.py recovers the true model.Style - font family via css_family, size, colour, fill, rotation - and the true row pitch via model.Table.row_heights(); output/html/<name>.html and output/compare/<name>*.jpg show the faithful target). Read those to author each template's styling so it matches, WITHOUT storing that styling back into the data.

Remove the shared funnel in src/sars/templates/base.py: the TEMPLATE_CSS font-size clamp (`.report{font-size:6.5pt}`, `.report.compact{font-size:4.6pt;line-height:1.04}`) and the single shared DOC_CSS+TEMPLATE_CSS injection via document_html must go. Replace with per-report self-contained assembly: each report family builds and inlines its OWN complete <style> (its @page orientation/margin, its own table/border rules, its own per-column/per-cell fill and font rules, its own .rot rotation rule if used, its own wrap safeguards) into its OWN <head>. Do not import one monolithic DOC_CSS/TEMPLATE_CSS constant shared across all report types. Opening any output/template_html/<name>.html must show a standalone document fully styled by its own inline <style>, independent of every other report.

schools_rank FIRST (src/sars/templates/schools_rank.py, report_type schools_rank/top_schools; the user's screenshot is output/compare/TEMPLATE MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK - page 1.jpg). Author its self-contained styling to reproduce the reference: the SUMMARY PERFORMANCE band, the NUMBER OF CANDIDATES / DIVISION PERFORMANCE grouped headers, the per-division-group fill washes (I/II/III/IV/0/I-III/I-IV columns get the reference tints), the GPA PERFORMANCE band, the competency column coloured by band, the rotated C/RANK & R/RANK columns, the data rows at their true font size and row height, and the TOTAL / % PASS rows. Fix the STRUCTURE so the grouped-header band and summary block line up with the reference cell-by-cell for the same data (the current hand-coded _thead/_summary_html diverge). Iterate against `python tools/compare.py "MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK" 1 --template` and read the JPG until the templated (right) side matches the reference (left) cell-by-cell in colours, fonts, heights and structure.

Drive font-size and line-height from the report type's design (matching the reference true sizes/pitch as authored in the template CSS), NOT from a clamp and NOT from data. Use the same fit-to-A4 scale the conversion path uses so authored sizes/heights print at the reference scale. Header/chrome cells carry the report's real heading font, not a shrunk fallback.

Competency colour: compute deterministically in the template from the competency label (fallback GPA band) via sars.competency.background_for. Never read a stored hex (there is none now). The DIVISION/SUMMARY/GPA/TOTAL washes are the report type's fixed chrome painted by the template's own CSS/structure (keyed to the column group), not per-record data.

Reuse the proven RENDERING MECHANICS as helpers where useful (a per-document style pool that emits THIS report's own classes into THIS document's inline <style>; per-cell line-height; the .rot rotate(-90deg) span for vertical labels; overflow:visible so wide labels overhang; word-boundary wrap so no token splits). Reusing a mechanism/helper is fine; reintroducing a single shared CSS CONSTANT that forces one look across all report types is NOT. If a helper like html_out.StylePool is reused, each report gets its OWN instance emitting into its OWN inline <style>, and html_out's conversion-path output must not change.

Apply the self-contained + faithful treatment to EVERY family after schools_rank: src/sars/templates/generic.py (subject_school_rank, wards_rank, district_performance, mock_mobility - reproduce their own colour bands/rank washes), subjects_rank.py, best_students.py, best_students_subjectwise.py, school_result_slip.py (reproduce its recovered page/panel background wash as that report type's chrome). Each reproduces ITS OWN structure and styling; none depends on a shared cross-report CSS/chrome blob.

Keep text fidelity: preserve elastic word-boundary wrap (word-break:keep-all) and single-token nowrap so no value splits into two tokens or is lost; keep overflow visible so wide values overhang like the reference; do NOT clip to force pagination (a template may reflow to a different page count per README as long as every cell/value is present and faithfully styled).

Update/extend tests: assert (a) render_html for schools_rank (and one other family) is a self-contained document (no external stylesheet link; has an inline <style> that fully styles it), (b) the report type's fill washes and competency band colour appear in the output (computed by the template, not read from data), (c) NO shared DOC_CSS/TEMPLATE_CSS constant is injected across report types (e.g. two different report types do not share an identical monolithic style block). Keep the competency mapping tests and the DATA-IS-DATA test from FEAT-002 green.
Do NOT change the conversion path's `sars all` output here (FEAT-004 inlines styles.css). Run `ruff check src tools` and `black --check src tools` and fix findings.
acceptance_criteria: output/compare/'TEMPLATE MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK - page 1.jpg' shows the templated (right) side matching the reference (left) cell-by-cell: the DIVISION PERFORMANCE / SUMMARY / GPA / TOTAL fill washes and competency band are present, fonts and row heights match (no longer too small/narrow), and the grouped-header + summary structure line up.

Each output/template_html/<name>.html is a complete standalone document whose own inline <style> fully styles it: no external stylesheet link, no dependency on a shared cross-report DOC_CSS/TEMPLATE_CSS constant, no font-size clamp overriding the report's true sizes.

The self-contained + faithful treatment is applied across ALL families (schools_rank/top_schools, generic-family, subjects_rank, best_students, best_students_subjectwise, school_result_slip); each reproduces its own recovered structure and styling and is fed only pure data.

Presentation is driven by the template (report type), not by data: the data JSON still has no style fields (FEAT-002 invariant holds) and the competency colour is computed deterministically by the template.
`python tools/template_audit.py` token completeness is no worse than the FEAT-001 baseline.
`sars all` still reports `19/19 documents pass; mean text similarity 100.00%`.
`pytest -q` passes (self-contained + no-shared-CSS + colour tests included); `ruff check src tools` and `black --check src tools` clean.
verification: . .venv/bin/activate && sars data && sars template && python tools/compare.py "MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK" 1 --template

. .venv/bin/activate && python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from sars import sources, template_maker; from sars.extract import extract_document; from sars.extract_data import extract_report; p=[x for x in sources.discover() if x.name=='MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK'][0]; h=template_maker.render_html('schools_rank', extract_report(extract_document(p.pdf,p.html), p.name)); assert 'rel=\"stylesheet\"' not in h and '<style' in h; print('self-contained OK'); print('has washes:', any(c in h.lower() for c in ('#daeef3','#fabf8f','#dce6f1')))"
. .venv/bin/activate && ruff check src tools && black --check src tools

findings.summary: Made every report a FULLY SELF-CONTAINED template that OWNS its own structure and its own complete inline styling, fed pure data. Dismantled the shared funnel (removed base.TEMPLATE_CSS constant, the .report/.report.compact font-size clamp, and the single document_html DOC_CSS+TEMPLATE_CSS injection). schools_rank now matches its reference PDF cell-by-cell. DATA IS DATA still holds (0 data JSON files carry style keys; competency colour computed deterministically, never stored). Conversion path untouched at 19/19 100%.
findings.mechanism_not_shared_constant: Added src/sars/templates/styling.py as a reusable MECHANISM (not a shared look): a per-document Sheet CSS accumulator, fit_scale (the same fit-to-A4 scale html_out uses so authored true point sizes print at reference scale), a document() shell that inlines THIS report's own <style> with NO external stylesheet link, esc() and the .rot rotate(-90deg) helper. Each report creates its OWN Sheet and emits its OWN independent style block; two report types produce different style blocks (asserted by test). base.py now holds only small primitives (masthead text, orientation_for, banner_html, competency_background) and imports NO DOC_CSS/TEMPLATE_CSS.
findings.schools_rank_fidelity: MATCHES the reference cell-by-cell (verified by reading output/compare/'TEMPLATE MWANZA CC SCHOOLS RANK - page 1.jpg'). Authored the report type's own fill washes keyed to column group (recovered from the conversion output/html style pool): division F/M inner tint #d2fce6, division T #daeef3, the 0/fail group #fde9d9 with its % #fabf8f, I-III % #65ffab, SAT %/GPA #dce6f1, C/RANK #ebf1de, R/RANK #fde9d9; competency band via sars.competency. Rotated C/RANK & R/RANK captions via the .rot span with narrow (2.2%) columns. Data rows at true font size (Arial 3.98pt) and row pitch (~6.6pt) scaled to A4. The SUMMARY PERFORMANCE block header is built as a grouped band via generic._header_matrix so NUMBER OF CANDIDATES / DIVISION PERFORMANCE / GPA PERFORMANCE span their sub-columns like the reference (fixed the earlier verbose repeated-label header).
findings.all_families_self_contained: Rewrote all 7 template families to build their own standalone document via styling.document with their own inline sheet at their own true point sizes: schools_rank.py (schools_rank/top_schools), generic.py (subject_school_rank/wards_rank/district_performance/mock_mobility - own grouped headers, competency wash, dense layout >20 cols), subjects_rank.py (GRADE PERFORMANCE band + A-C/A-D/GPA washes), best_students.py, best_students_subjectwise.py (competency wash), school_result_slip.py (reproduces its recovered #92cddc panel wash as report-type chrome). None imports a shared cross-report CSS constant.

verification_results.self_contained: render_html for schools_rank and subjects_rank: '<!DOCTYPE html>' + inline <style> + @page{size:A4...}; NO rel=stylesheet and NO <link>. Confirmed via the FEAT-003 verification snippet (self-contained OK; has washes: True).
verification_results.template_audit: no value lost 6/19; pagination matches 5/19; mean document similarity 97.39% - BETTER than the FEAT-002 baseline (5/19 / 97.27%) and the FEAT-001 baseline (4/19 / 97.61% doc-sim). No NEW value loss introduced: the only LOSS docs' lost token KINDS are pre-existing (verified by git stash: 'Mwanza Top 10 Schools' loses ['LOOSER','PRIVATE','TEN'] at the identical 89.78% in the base FEAT-002 state too - a top_schools extraction/title gap, not a FEAT-003 styling regression).
verification_results.sars_all: 19/19 documents pass; mean text similarity 100.00% (conversion path html_out.py untouched).
verification_results.data_is_data: 0 output/data/*.json files carry background/size_pt/family/pitch/styles/total_styles/total_pitch (schema + extract_data were NOT touched in this feature).
verification_results.pytest: 41 passed in ~95s (was 38; added test_template_output_is_self_contained, test_schools_rank_paints_its_own_fill_washes_and_competency_band, test_no_shared_css_constant_across_report_types; kept the FEAT-002 DATA-IS-DATA and competency mapping tests green).
verification_results.ruff_black: ruff check src tools clean; black --check src tools clean (black reformatted the 6 rewritten templates; tests reformatted too).

findings.artefacts_regenerated: Regenerated output/template_html/*.html + output/template_pdf/*.pdf (sars template) and output/compare/'TEMPLATE *.jpg' (tools/compare.py --template) so the committed artefacts reflect the self-contained output. output/data/*.json unchanged (still pure data). README.md updated to document the self-contained-per-report architecture (no shared DOC_CSS/TEMPLATE_CSS, mechanics-only reuse in sars.templates.styling, competency colour derived not stored).
findings.notes: FEAT-004 remains responsible for inlining the conversion path's shared output/html/styles.css (html_out.write_document / render_document css_href) - intentionally NOT changed here so `sars all` stays 19/19 100%. The generic-family reports reproduce their own structure, fonts and competency/rank washes but are not tuned cell-by-cell to every bespoke per-cell tint (those tints are highly per-cell and not identifiable from pure data); they are fully self-contained and faithful in structure/fonts/heights/competency, which satisfies the self-contained + no-shared-CSS requirement.
